review_notes: I read the whole file and the erase API in Corner.lean (mem_erase_iff, cells_erase, rowLen_erase, colLen_erase). I also read the hookLength definitions and simp set in HookLength/Basic.lean, and grepped the repo for uses of the hookLength_erase lemmas. The only use outside the declarations is `rw [h.hookLength_erase]` inside prod_hookLength_erase. The other lemmas (same_row, same_col, ne_row_ne_col) are not simp and are used only by `hookLength_erase`. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour. The finding is a judgement about interface design, not a proven failure. The row and column length lemmas in Corner.lean are intentionally simp and feed the proofs here; I found no loop or competing-rule problem there.

findings.excerpt:
@[simp]
theorem hookLength_erase (h : IsCorner μ c) (hd : d ∈ erase μ c) :
findings.problem: The combined pointwise lemma is tagged @[simp], but it has two substantive hypotheses: `IsCorner μ c` and `d ∈ erase μ c`. Its right-hand side is an `if` with a disjunctive condition and a truncated subtraction `hookLength μ d - 1`. Simp can only fire it if its discharger proves both hypotheses. The corner hypothesis is not a simp fact, and membership in `erase μ c` is not a normal-form fact either. When the hypotheses are available, it expands every `hookLength (erase μ c) d` into a branching term that hides the three cases proved just above. The sharper cases are not simp lemmas: `hookLength_erase_of_same_row`, `hookLength_erase_of_same_col` and `hookLength_erase_of_ne_row_of_ne_col`. Their `+ 1` and equality forms avoid truncated subtraction and are better targets once the row or column relation is known. The only use in the repo is the explicit `rw [h.hookLength_erase]` in `prod_hookLength_erase`, so the attribute gives no practical benefit. It only adds a surprising expansion to the global simp set.
findings.proposed_change: Drop `@[simp]` from `hookLength_erase` and keep it as a `rw`/`exact` lemma, as `prod_hookLength_erase` already uses it. If simp coverage is wanted, tag the unconditional-in-shape lemma `hookLength_erase_of_ne_row_of_ne_col` instead. Its hypotheses `d.1 ≠ c.1` and `d.2 ≠ c.2` are the kind simp can often discharge from the context, and its result is the unexpanded `hookLength μ d` with no `if`.
findings.benefit: This keeps the global simp set free of a doubly conditional rewrite that introduces `if` and `- 1`. Callers who want the case split get it explicitly, and simp normal forms for hook lengths stay predictable (`hookLength μ d` rather than a branch).

evidence.excerpt: hookLength (erase μ c) d = hookLength μ d
theorem mem_erase_iff (h : IsCorner μ c) : d ∈ erase μ c ↔ d ∈ μ ∧ d ≠ c
